title: Compare PI tuning methods without inventing a winner
equipment: Recirculating water heater, integrating buffer tank, and continuous belt dryer
physicalPurpose: Choose controller settings from method eligibility, common validation evidence, and explicit engineering preferences instead of a formula name or one attractive metric.
principalTechnique: Qualified SIMC and AMIGO PI comparison with Pareto trade-offs
objective: Use accepted models of three real industrial processes to decide which PI tuning methods are eligible, validate every real candidate under the same conditions, and conclude whether one candidate, several trade-off candidates, or no acceptable candidate meets the requirements.

simplifications: Independent plant copies isolate the tuning-method change
Locally linear accepted models within the declared operating regions
Equal deterministic sinusoidal sensor interference on equivalent copies
The tank valve lag is represented by the effective delay qualified in Lesson 44

baseline.limitation: One qualified method does not show whether another eligible published method offers a different response, robustness, or actuator-use trade-off.

change.decision: Retain eligibility, unavailability reasons, raw measures, failed requirements, and Pareto trade-offs without inventing a universal winner.

AMIGO.reason: AMIGO PI is unavailable for an integrating model because it requires finite steady plant gain and time constant.

disturbances: A minus-1-degC heater equilibrium shift at 100 s
A plus-1-percent tank outlet-flow-equivalent shift at 100 s
A minus-2-percent dryer equilibrium shift at 100 s
Separate bounded plant-gain and delay validation cases in Control Studio

acceptance.window: 10 through 100 s before the load event
10 through 220 s using common sampled IAE
10 through 220 s cumulative total variation minus heater SIMC total variation
10 through 220 s using common sampled IAE
10 through 220 s cumulative total variation minus dryer SIMC total variation

abortPredicates: Any required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
Any process value or applied output leaves its declared hard limit
Any plant, model revision, controller convention, initial state, sample interval, event, seed, limit, metric window, or uncertainty case differs between compared methods
A physical-plant target or Apply action is selected
safety.restorationMode: Disable the experiment and restart every simulated copy at its declared operating point before another candidate or variation.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer and responsible plant operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: This lesson cannot authorise physical excitation or gain application
Physical use requires independent topology, model, hazard, operating-window, interlock, personnel, abort, rollback, and immediate approval review

video.viewerOutcome: Separate tuning-method eligibility, candidate feasibility, and engineering preference while comparing real PI candidates without a hidden winner.
requiredVisibleEvidence: five executable controller and plant copies

learning.context: Equivalent simulated water-heater and dryer copies compare Balanced SIMC and AMIGO PI; the integrating tank executes only its eligible SIMC candidate.
learning.reason: A response target inside one tuning method does not resolve conflicting gains returned by another qualified method for the same accepted model.
theory: Method-domain eligibility determines whether a candidate may be created.
IAE, ISE, ITAE, transient, actuator, margin, and sensitivity measures expose different engineering costs.
Mandatory feasibility precedes Pareto preference, and an unavailable method is not ranked as a failed controller.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate both heater and dryer candidate gains, calculate the tank SIMC gains, predict the tank AMIGO unavailable result, and predict the direction of each error-versus-actuator trade-off before running.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, plant and model revisions, classes, units, quality, operating points, timing, limits, seed, events, methods, formulas, and unapplied state.
Declare common scenarios, raw metric equations, windows, validity rules, mandatory requirements, Pareto preference measures, and abort criteria before validation.
learning.baseline: Balanced SIMC supplies three qualified PI candidates but does not establish whether another eligible method offers a useful trade-off.
learning.change: Add AMIGO only where its model domain is satisfied and compare every real candidate with the unchanged validation plan.
learning.comparison: Change only method-derived Kp and Ki while retaining every plant, controller, timing, limit, event, noise, uncertainty, and calculation condition.
learning.validation: Classify availability and feasibility before preference; retain raw measures, requirements, margins, sensitivity peaks, and Pareto outcomes with no silent application.
learning.explanation: Method aggressiveness depends on plant parameters and delay ratio; one candidate may improve error while worsening actuator use or robustness, and an integrating model can make a method unavailable.
learning.transfer: Use eligibility, common validation, and explicit preference as separate decisions; Lesson 52 may automate the sequence only while keeping every decision inspectable and every candidate unapplied.
